title: Mouse Islet Perifusion (3-stimuli protocol)
author: Islet and Pancreas Analysis Core
materials: Prepare base perifusion media by combining reagents below in a 1-L Erlenmeyer flask. Add 1 L of deionized water and mix on a magnetic stir plate for at least 00:15:00 until dissolved. 3.2 g NaHCO3 Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #S6014-500G 0.58 g L-Glutamine Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #G8540-100G 0.11 g Sodium Pyruvate Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #P2256-25G 1.11 g HEPES Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #H7523 8.28 g DMEM Corning Catalog #90113 1 g RIA-grade BSA Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #A7888 70 mg L-Ascorbic acid Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #A5960 Base media can be made up to 24 hours before perifusion, and stored at 4 °C . All subsequent media must be made fresh.
Open the darkfield image in the cellSens software. Using the manual HSV threshold function, segment the islet tissue channel.
Restart intake pump until next secretagogue change.

steps.title: Prepare Media and Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the various glucose and secretagogue media required for perifusion.

substeps.instruction: Prepare islet picking media (HBSS with 10% FBS) by removing 50 mL from a 500-mL bottle of HBSS (Gibco #14025) and adding 50 mL FBS (Sigma #F0926).
Prepare 5.6 mM glucose media: add 0.5549 g Glucose (Fisher #D16) to 550 mL base perifusion media in a 500-mL bottle and mix until dissolved.
Prepare 16.7 mM high glucose media: add 0.7522 g Glucose (Fisher #D16) to 250 mL base perifusion media in a 250-mL bottle and mix until dissolved.
Prepare 5.6 mM glucose with 20 mM KCl: add 0.149 g Potassium chloride (Fisher #BP366-500) to 100 mL 5.6 mM glucose media.
Prepare 100 µM IBMX in 16.7 mM glucose media: weigh ~10 mg IBMX (Sigma #I5879), dissolve in 45 µL DMSO to make a 200 mM stock, then add 100 µL of this stock to 100 mL 16.7 mM glucose media.
Filter media using a vacuum-filtration system, transfer to a side-arm flask, and de-gas at 37 °C for at least 00:30:00.
Wait 00:30:00 and verify glucose levels using a glucose meter.
Reserve 30 mL 5.6 mM glucose media in a 50-mL conical tube for islet loading and unloading.

steps.title: Set Up Perifusion System
steps.instruction: Prepare the hardware, water bath, and gas lines for the perifusion run.

substeps.instruction: Fill perifusion water bath with deionized water to about 1 inch from the top and set temperature to 37 °C.
Place media bottles in the water bath to warm for at least 00:10:00.
Replace Pyrex orange caps with 4-Luer (+1) caps on all media bottles and tape over holes to prevent gas escape.
Turn on gas (95% O2, 5% CO2) and insert one gas line into each bottle cap (suspended above the liquid); block remaining holes with tape.
Rinse tubing with deionized water at max pump speed for 00:15:00, then place new frits into the islet chamber.
Label perifusion tubes (date, islet type, fraction number) and load them into the fraction collector trays.

steps.title: Islet Selection and Sizing
steps.instruction: Handpick and size islets to meet the required Islet Equivalent (IEQ) for the specific assay.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 6-cm dish with 5 mL islet picking media for each channel.
Place freshly-isolated mouse islets on an inverted microscope stage; view with 4x objective and size using the 10x eyepiece reticle.
Handpick islets using a 200-µL micropipette and transfer to the 6-cm dish.
Record islet number and size to calculate IEQ (Target: 50-70 IEQ for insulin secretion [Mercodia #10-1247-10]; 150-200 IEQ for glucagon secretion [Mercodia #10-1281-01]).
Transfer all islets from the center of the dish to a clear 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tube for loading.

steps.title: Load Islets into Chamber
steps.instruction: Transfer the islets into the perifusion chamber while ensuring no air bubbles are present.

substeps.instruction: Place intake catheters into baseline media bottle (resting on bottom). Run baseline media through chambers at max pump speed for ~00:10:00 and discard flow-through.
Ensure intake and air uptake pumps are off; open the air uptake waste pathway stopcock and close the fraction collector outlet stopcock.
Remove the chamber from mounting, turn it upside down, remove the red end piece (inlet), and discard two-thirds of the media.
Using a 1-mL micropipette, transfer the islet slurry from the microcentrifuge tube to the chamber, rinsing the tube 3 times with baseline media.
Place chamber back on mounting and fill with baseline media until a convex meniscus forms. Tap sides to dislodge bubbles and remove bubbles from the top.
Carefully replace the inlet plunger without introducing bubbles.
Turn the chamber right side up on the mounting rack. Open the fraction collector outlet line and close the air uptake waste line.

steps.title: Execute Perifusion Protocol
steps.instruction: Run the perifusion sequence, collecting fractions based on the stimuli protocol.

substeps.instruction: Tighten column end pieces and fittings to ensure no leaks. Lower the mounting rack into the water bath and tighten the clamp.
Turn on intake and air uptake pumps. Set fraction collector to 00:03:00, position the arm over the first tube, and press 'Start'.
Record each intake pump speed in the perifusion logbook.
Collect 10 preliminary fractions using 5.6 mM glucose media (1 mL/min delivery, 3 mL per fraction) to rinse islets and synchronize pump speed.
Collect subsequent fractions, changing media/secretagogues at predetermined timepoints. Pause the intake pump when the collector moves at the desired timepoint.
Move media intake catheters from one secretagogue to the next, ensuring catheters rest on the bottom and tubing is not tangled.

steps.title: Post-Perifusion Recovery and Storage
steps.instruction: Stop the system and recover islets for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Stop intake and air uptake pumps and close stopcocks to air uptake and media outlet lines.
Cap perifusion fractions and store at -20 °C.
Raise the mounting rack from the water bath and wait ~00:02:00 for islets to settle.
Carefully remove the blue outlet end piece. Pipet islets and media into a 6-cm untreated tissue culture dish; rinse the chamber and blue end piece 5 times with 1 mL baseline media into the dish.
Transfer all islets from the dish to a clear 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Islet Quantification and Extraction
steps.instruction: Perform imaging and hormone extraction on recovered islets.

substeps.instruction: Perform imaging: Place the dish on a stereomicroscope (10x magnification). Capture brightfield (12 ms exposure) and darkfield (400 ms exposure) images using cellSens software. Save files.
Use the 'Count and Measure' algorithm to determine islet count and mean diameter, using 'Manually Split Objects' for discrete islets.
Assign islets to diameter groups based on the provided chart to calculate recovered IEQ (Expected retrieval rate ~93%).
Centrifuge the islet tube at 200 rcf for 3 minutes; aspirate supernatant and place tube on ice.
Prepare fresh acid alcohol: add 50 µL 12M HCl to 5.5 mL 95% ethanol.
Add 200 µL acid ethanol to the islet pellet and incubate at 4 °C overnight (up to 24:00:00).
Centrifuge tube at 3000 rpm for 5 minutes; transfer three 50 µL aliquots of supernatant to 2-mL screwcap tubes and store at -80 °C.

steps.title: System Cleanup
steps.instruction: Decontaminate and rinse the perifusion system.

substeps.instruction: Turn off intake and air uptake pumps, drain the water bath, and turn off gas.
Rinse all lines (including waste) with deionized water at max pump speed for ~01:30:00.
Reassemble column and rinse all lines (including waste) with 10% bleach at max pump speed for ~00:15:00.
Rinse the chamber with deionized water and remove frits.
Record date, details, and any errors in the perifusion logbook.

steps.title: Final Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform insulin and/or glucagon assays on the collected perifusion fractions and extracts.
